title: Loose pieces

D0.outcome: Says that in this course a loose piece is one that an enemy piece attacks and none of its own side defends, and why it is in danger.

D1.outcome: When told 'find the loose pieces', taps every attacked piece that has no defender (kings do not count).

D2.outcome: With no announcement, says how many of its pieces are loose, including none.

D3.outcome: Before each move checks both sides' pieces, and notices pieces that become loose only after a move or an exchange.

misconceptions: A piece is safe because nothing attacks it right now.
A defended piece can never be lost.
A piece nobody attacks is in danger just because nothing defends it.
conditions: A piece is loose when an enemy piece attacks it and none of its own side's pieces defends it.
Check the pieces one by one; kings are not counted.
contrasts: A piece that is attacked but defended is not loose, although the exchange may still go against it (see SAF.COUNT).
A piece that nobody attacks is not loose even if nothing defends it.
